title: Orsen and the Protocol
premise: Mara Underhill, an insurance investigator who documents the slow, unfunded decay of the colony Meridian's Rest, discovers a name on the manifest of a ship that never launched: Orsen Vey, a child registered as crew of a vessel that exists only in falsified records. The 'Orsen Protocol' turns out to be a decades-old deception—a fake evacuation fleet maintained in paperwork to keep two rival orbital fleets from fighting over the dying colony. When both fleets arrive to claim the truth, Mara must keep the lie alive long enough for the colonists' real evacuation to finish, sacrificing their own reputation and falling in love with Orsen's guardian, engineer Sefa Ilo. In the end, the reactor countdown reaches zero as the last shuttle clears, and Mara chooses found family over career, staying behind-recorded, invisible, and finally home.
about_author: Bram Ishikawa is the pen name of a former maritime claims adjuster who spent eleven years investigating losses at sea before turning to fiction. They write quiet, procedural science fiction about people whose jobs are to witness disasters rather than survive them.

chapters.title: The Actuary of Small Catastrophes
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Underhill arrives at Meridian's Rest to assess a collapsing water reclamation plant, cataloguing leaks, rust, and the colony's dwindling population like entries in a ledger. A local girl asks if anyone will read the report. Emotional beat: professional detachment cracking into unease—Mara realizes no one at the insurer expects the colony to exist in five years.

chapters.title: Manifest of a Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Cross-referencing colonial records against fleet registries, Mara finds the name Orsen Vey listed as crew on the ISV Halcyon Step—a vessel logged as evacuated the colony forty years ago but which no port ever recorded docking. Emotional beat: the thrill of an anomaly, quickly shadowed by the sense of touching something deliberately buried.

chapters.title: Sefa Keeps the Lights On
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Colony engineer Sefa Ilo maintains the reactor and lies to her neighbors about how much time it has left. She notices the investigator asking dangerous questions and decides to charm them rather than fight them. Emotional beat: weary tenderness—she protects this place because it's all anyone bothered to leave her.

chapters.title: Orsen
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Mara finally meets Orsen Vey: not a ghost, but a quiet teenager raised on station stories, whose identity was grafted onto the phantom ship's manifest to give him legal existence. He doesn't know what his name is worth. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread as Mara understands someone built a person out of paperwork.

chapters.title: The Protocol
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Sefa reveals the Orsen Protocol to Mara in confidence: two rival fleets—the Concord and the Verity Compact—each believe the other has a binding claim on the colony, frozen in place by forged manifests neither side dares audit. The lie is the only peace treaty. Emotional beat: the weight of inherited secrets; Sefa asks Mara to become a co-conspirator.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Won't Say
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Mara drafts an honest report and deletes it, then files a deliberately bland one instead, feeling their integrity bend. Meanwhile they trace who forged the original manifest—and find their own predecessor's signature. Emotional beat: complicity; the first deliberate act of deception, done gently, for strangers.

chapters.title: Harvest of Rust
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Orsen scavenges the dead districts with his friend Pell, mapping parts Sefa needs. He finds a sealed Concord drop-capsule from decades past, still transmitting a handshake signal. Emotional beat: adolescent bravado giving way to fear—he's just handed the outside world a door back in.

chapters.title: Handshake
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. The capsule's signal pings a Concord relay; within days, a survey drone enters orbit. Sefa scrambles to spoof colonial telemetry while the reactor throws its first unplanned shutdown. Emotional beat: controlled panic—she realizes the protocol has a clock now, and so does the reactor.

chapters.title: Two Flags Over a Dying Town
chapters.summary: POV Mara. A Concord liaison arrives under cover of an insurance audit, probing Mara's reports for inconsistencies. Mara performs the role of bored bureaucrat while privately calculating how long the fiction can hold. Emotional beat: loneliness inside the lie—Mara can trust almost no one and is starting to mind.

chapters.title: The Verity Compact Learns to Count
chapters.summary: POV Mara. A Compact delegation lands uninvited, having independently noticed the manifest anomaly. Both fleets' agents circle each other in the colony's single cantina while colonists serve drinks and pretend deafness. Emotional beat: farce tightening into menace; Mara sees the war the lie has been preventing.

chapters.title: Pell's Question
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Pell, furious at being kept ignorant, nearly tells a Compact officer everything about the capsule. Orsen stops him—not with authority, but by finally telling the truth about what his own name means. Emotional beat: Orsen choosing guardianship over grievance; the found family consolidates around the secret.

chapters.title: Audit
chapters.summary: POV Mara. The Concord liaison presents Mara with evidence of the forgery and offers immunity in exchange for testimony that would hand the colony to the Compact's rivals—or rather, to the Concord. Mara stalls, buying days, and understands they are now the protocol's load-bearing wall. Emotional beat: temptation and refusal; duty inverted.

chapters.title: Reactor Song
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Sefa and Orsen perform improvised repairs inside the containment ring while she teaches him the reactor's rhythms like a lullaby. She admits the true evacuation plan: a ragged flotilla of refitted hulks, ready in weeks, able to carry everyone once—if—the fleets stand down. Emotional beat: fierce maternal love braided with fatalism.

chapters.title: The Countdown Becomes Public
chapters.summary: POV Mara. A coolant failure forces Sefa to announce the reactor's real timeline publicly: ninety-one days. Panic ripples through the colony; both fleet delegations smell leverage. Emotional beat: the private deadline becomes a weapon pointed at everyone; Mara watches the lie strain under honest arithmetic.

chapters.title: What Each Fleet Believes
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Working both delegations separately, Mara feeds each side a version of the truth: that the other fleet's claim rests on the same forged manifest, and that exposure means mutual disgrace and open war over a rock worth nothing. Emotional beat: exhausted diplomacy; Mara discovers they're good at this and hates it.

chapters.title: Orsen Signs His Name
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. The fleets demand the 'original crew heir' authenticate the disputed manifest. Orsen, coached overnight, stands before both delegations and claims his paper identity fully—testifying to a voyage he never took, making the lie legally true. Emotional beat: coming-of-age as self-sacrifice; he becomes the story invented for him.

chapters.title: Ninety-One to Zero
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. With the fleets locked in stalemate, the evacuation flotilla launches early and half-ready. Sefa runs the reactor past every safety margin to power the lift sequence, burning the station's future as fuel. Emotional beat: grim triumph—every hour bought by the lie is spent in steel and sweat.

chapters.title: The Lie Holds, Barely
chapters.summary: POV Mara. The Concord, unwilling to be disgraced alone, formally 'verifies' the manifest; the Compact follows suit. War is postponed by mutual blackmail. But the liaison leaves Mara one parting warning: auditors will come eventually. Emotional beat: hollow victory; Mara saves thousands and feels the cost settle into their bones.

chapters.title: Last Shuttle
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Final evacuation. Mara stays to certify the last manifests—officially required, secretly chosen—as Sefa and Orsen refuse to board without them. The three ride the final shuttle up together as the reactor's containment begins its terminal cascade. Emotional beat: love against duty resolved; Mara chooses the family that stayed.

chapters.title: Zero
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. From the flotilla's lead hulk, they watch Meridian's Rest go dark—not in fire, but in a slow, dignified shutdown Sefa scripted herself. Behind them, two fleets hold position, each waiting for the other to move, and neither does. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into release; the colony ends on its own terms.

chapters.title: The Report No One Reads
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Weeks later aboard the flotilla, Mara files the true account of the Orsen Protocol—then seals it for fifty years, protecting the fragile peace the fleets still pretend is legitimate. Orsen asks if hiding the truth was wrong. Mara says they'll both decide again when it opens. Emotional beat: moral ambiguity accepted with humility.

chapters.title: Course, Set Together
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. The flotilla plots a course toward an unclaimed system, a fleet of nobodies becoming a nation. Orsen, legally the heir of a ship that never flew, renames the convoy after it. Sefa and Mara stand beside him at the helm. Emotional beat: inheritance reclaimed—what was a lie becomes a legacy; found family becomes a future.
